Executive Overview

A half-century of compounding — key takeaways at a glance

Over its 53+ year trading history, American Express has delivered a 24,895% cumulative return, turning a $10,000 investment in 1972 into approximately $2,499,487 by March 2026 (split/dividend-adjusted basis). The compound annual growth rate of 10.81% significantly outpaces inflation over the same period, demonstrating AXP's durable wealth-creation capacity.

The stock's journey has been punctuated by severe drawdowns — most notably the 2008 Global Financial Crisis, which erased over 84% of AXP's value from peak to trough — yet each time the company recovered to new all-time highs. The current all-time high stands at $384.04 (reached on 2025-12-11), while the all-time adjusted low of $0.38 dates to 1974-10-03.

American Express has paid $34.27 in cumulative dividends per share, reinforcing its profile as an income-generating holding for long-term investors. The stock split history includes 6 split event(s), detailed in the Dividends & Splits section below.

Data & Methodology Notes

  • All prices are split- and dividend-adjusted, meaning historical prices are retroactively restated to reflect subsequent splits and distributions. The 1972 closing price of ~$1.22 does not represent the nominal price at that time.
  • CAGR is computed as (End Price / Start Price)1/Years − 1 using adjusted closing prices only. It does not include dividend reinvestment.
  • Maximum Drawdown is the largest peak-to-trough decline measured from a running cumulative maximum of the adjusted close.
  • Annualized Volatility is the standard deviation of daily log-returns multiplied by √252.
  • Early data (1972–~1983) shows identical OHLC values and zero volume, indicating only closing prices were available. Volatility metrics for this period may understate true price risk.
  • Dividend yield proxy is calculated as annual dividends per share divided by the average closing price for that year — it is an approximation, not the exact forward yield.
  • Data source: Kaggle dataset "American Express (AXP) Stock Data (1972–2026)" by anadiskt. The dataset contains 13,556 daily records across 8 columns.
